Subject: MSA redlines — publicity & confidentiality

Hi Stephanie,

Attached are our redlines to the MSA and the draft order form — primarily focused on publicity and logo use. A few items we want clarified from Redwood before we move to signature: 

- Quiet period / embargo language: we asked for a 90-day embargo after launch for marketing collateral to avoid pre-announcement leaks.
- Logo use: we prefer logos to be used only in case studies with prior written approval and brand guide compliance.
- Reference rights: we want a limited reference clause that allows Redwood to list BrightLane as a customer but not to publish customer quotes without separate approval.

Can you confirm Redwood's standard positions on (1) embargo windows and (2) whether you can accept a written-approval gating process for logo assets? We can be flexible on short press mentions but need firm controls on logos and quotes.

Thanks — attaching BrightLane_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf.

Regards,
Sarah Park
Sr. Procurement Manager, BrightLane

Hi Sarah — thanks for sending this over and for the clear callouts. Looping in Rishi (legal) and Laura (sales ops) to review the redlines. A few quick items from my side so we can expedite: 

- Embargo/quiet-period: Redwood typically defaults to a 30-day notice before public announcements tied to a joint customer launch. We can evaluate a 90-day request but will need to confirm product launch dependencies and PR coordination.
- Logo usage: We are comfortable with "logo by approval" but prefer a single approval process (one person at BrightLane) and a limited permission window (e.g., 12 months) with automatic renewal on request.
- Quotes/Case studies: We accept a two-step approval for quotes — we can redact and send for approval within 3 business days and won't publish without explicit sign-off.

Rishi / Laura — can you review Sarah's redlines and propose carve language we can send back to BrightLane that balances their ask with Redwood's go-to-market requirements? From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: MSA redlines — publicity & confidentiality

Thanks for the loop. I reviewed BrightLane's redlines and propose the following practical language and approach — aim is to protect the customer's confidentiality while allowing Redwood to maintain a predictable reference/marketing program.

1) Quiet-period (proposed):
"Customer and Redwood agree that neither party will make public announcements specifically referring to the other party's products, services, or the relationship for a period of ninety (90) days following the Effective Date of the applicable Order Form, unless both parties provide prior written consent. For avoidance of doubt, this sentence does not prevent private customer communications or filings required by law."

Comment: We can accept 90 days if BrightLane owns coordinating the launch date notification and agrees to a single-point approval contact. Otherwise standard is 30 days.

2) Logo and asset usage (proposed):
"Redwood may request permission to use Customer's name and logo for marketing and reference purposes. Use of Customer logos or reproductions of branding assets shall require Customer's prior written approval, which Customer will not unreasonably withhold. Customer agrees to provide a designated approver and shall respond to logo usage requests within ten (10) business days. Approved use is limited to the specific assets and contexts described in the approval communication and will expire twelve (12) months from the date of approval unless renewed in writing."

3) Quotes and case studies (proposed):
"Redwood may propose customer quotes or case study materials to Customer. Customer shall have at least five (5) business days to review and approve any proposed quote or case study excerpt. Redwood will not publish Customer quotes without Customer's explicit written consent, which may be withheld or conditioned by Customer."

4) Audit trail and evidence: we recommend adding an exhibit listing the approver contact and an audit log clause to record approvals (email thread or shared drive link).

If those clauses look acceptable to BrightLane, we will prepare tracked changes on the MSA and a clean copy of the Order Form. If BrightLane insists on longer approval response windows or different renewal mechanics, flag specifics and we can escalate.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
